statement: A city has n intersections, numbered 0 to n − 1. graph holds the count n and a list of roads [u, v, time]; each road can be driven in both directions and takes the given time. Every intersection can be reached from every other.
Consider the routes from intersection 0 to intersection n − 1 whose total time is the smallest possible.
Return how many different such shortest routes exist. Because the count can be very large, return it modulo 10⁹ + 7.

examples.explanation: The shortest time from 0 to 6 is 7, and four routes achieve it: the direct road 0 − 6, 0 − 4 − 6, 0 − 1 − 2 − 5 − 6 and 0 − 1 − 3 − 5 − 6.
There is only one road, so the single route 0 − 1 with time 10 is the only shortest one.

constraints: at most one road joins any two intersections
every intersection can be reached from every other
